newsitem.title: USA: DC finance chief sees job, pay, welfare cuts ahead.
newsitem.headline: DC finance chief sees job, pay, welfare cuts ahead.

text.p: District of Columbia's government is going to have to cut jobs, pay and welfare benefits to help achieve $85.4 million in savings, the city's chief financial officer said Monday.

"You're talking about...on the personnel side in terms of unfortunately, reduction in wages, benefit levels, adjustments in terms of management as well," Anthony Williams said on Fox TV's "Fox Morning News."
He added, "You're talking about on the non-personnel side a whole range of different initiatives being reconfigured so that they work better and actually achieve the savings we wanted."

Williams was speaking two days after the head of the D.C. financial control board, Andrew Brimmer, said he would ask the board to order the District to cut benefits to workers and welfare recipients to reach the target for savings soon.
Williams said that the embattled district government would have to cut welfare benefits possibly by three percent in order to put them more in line with neighboring areas.
"Here what you're talking about doing, you have the number of people you have on the rolls, but you reduce the amount of benefits that person may get," he said.
